name: Prenatal Complete Gummies
reasoningTemplate: This is exactly the kind of prenatal formula obstetricians like to see — folate, iron, vitamin D, DHA and choline, with no red flags.

name: Tylenol Extra Strength
reasoningTemplate: For everyday aches and fever, this is the pain reliever providers reach for first at every stage.

name: Advil Ibuprofen 200 mg
reasoningTemplate: This one changes with your calendar — NSAIDs like ibuprofen are treated very differently in the third trimester than earlier on.

name: Midnight Renewal Retinol Serum 0.5%
reasoningTemplate: Retinoids are the one skincare family dermatologists consistently ask pregnant patients to shelve.

name: Glow Barrier Niacinamide Serum
reasoningTemplate: A bump-friendly glow: every active in this bottle has a clean record in pregnancy and nursing.

name: Cold Brew Black Coffee
reasoningTemplate: Good news first: you don't have to give this up — it's about the daily total.

name: Chunk Light Tuna in Water
reasoningTemplate: Fish is genuinely good for the baby's brain — the mercury math is what needs watching.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon 2021
reasoningTemplate: This is the clearest call in the whole database — there's no established safe amount of alcohol in pregnancy.

name: Salon Color Lasting Nail Lacquer
reasoningTemplate: Classic three-free offenders — this formula still carries the old-school solvents modern polishes dropped.

name: Sport Clear Sunscreen SPF 50
reasoningTemplate: Sunscreen itself is encouraged — it's this particular UV filter that's worth swapping out.

name: Pure Mineral SPF 50
reasoningTemplate: Mineral filters sit on top of the skin instead of absorbing in — the go-to recommendation during pregnancy.

name: Double Crème Brie
reasoningTemplate: Soft-ripened cheeses are a listeria question — and the answer hinges on pasteurization.

name: Milk Flow Lactation Tea
reasoningTemplate: A nursing-era classic — traditional galactagogues with a mixed but mostly reassuring evidence base.

name: Deep Woods Insect Repellent
reasoningTemplate: Counterintuitive but true: DEET is recommended in pregnancy — the mosquito-borne illnesses it prevents are the real risk.
